bottom_line.text: Laparoscopic repair reduces chronic postoperative pain compared with Lichtenstein repair [90000001; 90000002; 90000003]. The absolute benefit is mainly in mild pain [90000004]. One long-term trial found no difference at about 8 years [90000007].
bottom_line.certainty_reason: Consistent direction across overlapping meta-analyses, but pain definitions vary and trials are open-label.

at_a_glance:
Laparoscopic repair causes less chronic pain than Lichtenstein repair [90000001; 90000002].
- Chronic pain: RR 0.38 with TEP vs Lichtenstein [90000001]
- Chronic pain at 5 years: 9.4% with TEP vs 18.8% with Lichtenstein [90000004]
- Recurrence: RR 1.03, no difference [90000001]
Main caveat: pain definitions vary and trials are open-label.
clinical_practice:
Default choice: Offer TEP or TAPP when a surgeon experienced in it is available [90000001; 90000002]. Lichtenstein remains a sound repair when laparoscopic expertise is lacking [90000005].
Who may benefit: Patients most concerned about chronic pain [90000004].
Counselling: Fewer people have lasting groin pain after keyhole repair; recurrence is similar [90000001].
Cost per case: not known
